nodes.summary: The Steiner ratio constant, the infimum over finite sets $V$ of at least two points in the Euclidean plane of the length of a Steiner minimal tree for $V$ divided by the length of a minimum spanning tree of $V$, is at least $0.824$.
nodes.title: Chung–Graham lower bound for the Steiner ratio

nodes.summary: For points $x$ and $y$ of the Euclidean plane, the length of the unordered pair $\{x, y\}$ is the Euclidean distance between $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: Length of an edge

nodes.summary: The Steiner ratio of the Euclidean plane, that is, the infimum of the ratio of the Steiner minimal tree length to the minimum spanning tree length over all finite sets of at least two points in the plane, equals $\sqrt{3}/2$.
nodes.title: Gilbert–Pollak conjecture

nodes.summary: The Steiner ratio constant, the infimum over finite sets $V$ of at least two points in the Euclidean plane of the length of a Steiner minimal tree for $V$ divided by the length of a minimum spanning tree of $V$, is at most $\sqrt{3}/2$.
nodes.title: Gilbert–Pollak upper bound for the Steiner ratio

nodes.summary: For a finite set $V$ of points in the Euclidean plane, the minimum spanning tree length of $V$ is the infimum of the total lengths of the trees with vertex set $V$. For nonempty $V$ this set of lengths is finite and nonempty, so the infimum is a minimum; for empty $V$ the value is $0$ by convention.
nodes.title: Minimum spanning tree length

nodes.summary: The space $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the Euclidean distance, in which the point sets of the Steiner ratio problem lie.
nodes.title: The Euclidean plane of the Steiner ratio problem

nodes.summary: For a finite set $V$ of points in the Euclidean plane, this is the set of real numbers $\ell$ such that some tree with vertex set $V$ has total length $\ell$, the total length being the sum of the Euclidean lengths of its edges.
nodes.title: Lengths of spanning trees

nodes.summary: For every nonempty finite set $V$ of points in the Euclidean plane, the Steiner minimal tree length of $V$ is at most the minimum spanning tree length of $V$: allowing Steiner points never increases the optimal length.
nodes.title: The Steiner length is at most the minimum spanning tree length

nodes.summary: For a finite set $V$ of points in the Euclidean plane, the Steiner length of $V$ is the infimum of the total lengths of the trees whose vertex set is a finite set of points of the plane containing $V$. This set of lengths is nonempty and bounded below by $0$, so the infimum exists.
nodes.title: Steiner minimal tree length

nodes.summary: The Steiner ratio constant is the infimum, over all finite sets $V$ of at least two points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, of the ratio of the Steiner minimal tree length of $V$ to the minimum spanning tree length of $V$.
nodes.title: The Steiner ratio of the Euclidean plane

nodes.summary: For a finite set $V$ of points in the Euclidean plane, this is the set of real numbers $\ell$ such that, for some finite set $W$ of points of the plane containing $V$, some tree with vertex set $W$ has total length $\ell$. The points of $W$ outside $V$ are the Steiner points.
nodes.title: Lengths of Steiner trees

nodes.summary: For a finite set $V$ of points in the Euclidean plane and a simple graph $G$ with vertex set $V$, the total length of $G$ is the sum, over all edges $\{x, y\}$ of $G$, of the Euclidean distance between $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: Total length of a graph on points of the plane

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
